resolution_raising:
Status: every raise below is conditioned on the resolution failing closed. Anything that cannot be resolved stays exactly as it is today.

(1) R4-r4-2: `req: Model` becomes `Obj((C,), fields)`. Each field becomes MODEL/opaque → MODEL/resolved, with a per-field root such as `req.path`; nesting is limited to depth 2. Examples: write_model / write_dc / write_nt / nested / inherited / write_xmod / argv_field, and in the field check odoo_* got root refinement.
Why resolved is justified: FastMCP (the official SDK and jlowin fastmcp) validates arguments with pydantic using the annotation and constructs the instance. If no construction-time hook exists anywhere in the class family, each field holds the model's JSON value as-is, which is the same basis on which a plain parameter or a dict subscript is resolved. All of the following must hold:
 (a) The head name of the annotation is bound exactly once at module level (_module_bindings). Relative imports and in-tree modules are followed through their bindings; an external name counts only if it comes from a level-0 import that points outside the tree.
 (b) Every class in the family is either a strictly resolved in-tree class or the root pydantic.BaseModel / typing.NamedTuple. A dataclass may have only @dataclass-family class decorators. External bases, Generic[T], metaclass= and any other class decorator mean no seed.
 (c) The class counts as hooked if any of the following appears:
  - a method decorator other than those resolved to builtins property/classmethod/staticmethod, functools.cached_property, abc.abstractmethod, typing.override, or pydantic computed_field/field_serializer/model_serializer (a validator imported under an alias or wrapped by an in-tree function is caught this way; @x.setter is also hooked);
  - a definition of __init__, __new__, __post_init__, model_post_init, __setattr__, __getattribute__, __getattr__, __init_subclass__, model_validate*, model_construct, parse_*, construct, or any __get_pydantic*;
  - an assignment in the class body containing a call (the reuse pattern field_validator("x")(f));
  - class-body statements other than def / class / assignment / docstring (for example validators defined under if PYDANTIC_V2);
  - str_to_lower / str_strip_whitespace and similar in model_config, class Config or class keywords, or a model_config whose contents cannot be read (a name reference, ** expansion);
  - Annotated metadata other than Field(...) or strings, calls such as constr(...), aliases that may contain validators, names that cannot be resolved, or fields typed as in-tree classes that are themselves hooked;
  - in a dataclass, a call default other than field / Field (it could be a descriptor);
  - a write to the class name from anywhere in the tree (C.x = ... / setattr(C, ...)).
 (d) Not treated as fields: ClassVar, InitVar, names starting with _, PrivateAttr, init=False, and names that are also bound in the family by a def or an unannotated assignment. Reads of these attributes fall back to the base prin with opaque, so they stay MODEL/opaque as today.
 (e) Applied only to units whose framework is mcp or fastmcp.
 Points I think an attack should go after:
  - Types that change the value at construction (SecretStr and similar) are not treated as hooks.
  - Validators implicitly registered by pydantic plugins, or through an external type's __get_pydantic_core_schema__, are not seen.
  - An alias assignment `x = req; x.path = C` does not change req.path. That error goes toward a false alarm.

(2) R4-r1-6: `p: Path` changes shape from Atom to Path(base=MODEL/resolved Atom). prin, prov and roots are unchanged, so a pathlib.Path.* FS_WRITE row newly appears.
Why this is justified: the result is the same shape as constructing Path(path). It applies only when the annotation (with Optional, `| None` and string annotations unwrapped) resolves strictly to pathlib.Path / PosixPath / WindowsPath through the rule in (a). Annotated[Path, ...] is out of scope. An in-tree class Path, a relative import, an in-tree module, or two bindings mean no change.
 Point to attack: the code relies on the value being a Path, but a framework that passes the value through without coercing it would hand over a str. Even then, the write_text call itself would fail at runtime, so this is not a false-clean.

(3) R4-r4-1: a new env key <ctx>.request_context.lifespan_context / <server>.request_context.lifespan_context is set to the lifespan's yield value after _opaque_deep. Receiver types become available, so new DB / NET / SPAWN rows appear. The prov of the value itself is kept opaque, so this does not raise resolution: a constant stays unreadable (ce_lifespan_rebound stays 不). Constants and MODEL values inside the tool body, such as `"DELETE..." + item_id`, remain resolved as before.
 Conditions, all required:
  - The binding of the decorator receiver name is exactly one assignment, at module level or in the body of the enclosing module-level function. It must not be a parameter, global or nonlocal, and for the enclosing-function case the constructor names must not be rebound in that function.
  - The constructor resolves strictly to FastMCP (for tool) or Server (for call_tool).
  - lifespan= is a Name, and that name resolves strictly to an in-tree function decorated with @asynccontextmanager or @contextmanager.
  - No write to recv.*lifespan* exists after construction.
  - recv never appears as an argument to mount or import_server anywhere in the tree.
  - The ctx annotation resolves strictly to the mcp or fastmcp Context (Context[...] is accepted), and neither ctx nor server is rebound inside the tool.
  - The yield value's shape is known: no seed if it is Unknown.
 The lifespan body is evaluated by a separate engine with on_call=None, so startup effects are not attached to tools.
 Point to attack: prin becomes OP, so a path from ctx becomes OP/opaque instead of MODEL/opaque. I checked this in scratch against the D17 module-level shared dict: D2 fs_writeout / spawn_command / D3 net_host_unknown all stay 不, the same as the module-level case. The reasons, however, change from *_model_opaque to non-model ones, and INJECT-coordinate rows rooted at ctx disappear, which fix_outline (4) anticipates.

(4) langroid message_fields: resolution goes down (resolved → opaque) only for classes that have hooks.
